requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The change stops the analyzer from throwing inside TypeCollector when a [MessagePackObject] type has duplicate keys or mixes int and string keys. After reporting MsgPack005 on a mixed-key member, it now skips that member (`continue`). It no longer calls Dictionary.Add for a key that is already present. The same edits are made in two loops (lines ~1003-1043 and ~1144-1183). It also adds analyzer tests for SuppressSourceGeneration types, two execution tests for a suppressed type, and a README section on opting out.
story.why: The issue says the analyzer stops working for SuppressSourceGeneration = true types since 3.1.1. The diff's implied theory is that the analyzer crashed on these types: Dictionary.Add threw on duplicate keys, or `intKey!.Value` was dereferenced as null on mixed keys. That crash suppressed all diagnostics. The diff does not show any code that branches on SuppressSourceGeneration. Whether this crash is the whole cause of the issue cannot be confirmed from the visible lines.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new 'Opting out of source generation' section listing which rules apply to suppressed types.

TypeCollector.cs line 1007 replaces `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?` with `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. This is unrelated to the fix, and the parallel line 1147 was not changed the same way.
The crash fixes also change behaviour for normal (non-suppressed) [MessagePackObject] types, which share the same code path.
Execution tests check run-time round-trip and that no formatter is generated. This is runtime behaviour, not analyzer behaviour.
story.confidence_overview: High that the guards and `continue` prevent the two exceptions in the property-like loop, which the new property-based tests cover. Medium that this is the root cause of REQ-2234, since no suppression-specific code is visible. Low coverage for the second loop (lines 1144-1183, which looks like the field path): no new test uses fields with duplicate or mixed keys. Line 1007's `[0]` indexing is a new crash risk.

claims.text: Line 1007 now reads the diagnostic location with DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] instead of FirstOrDefault()?. This throws if the member has no syntax reference, for example an inherited member from metadata.
In the second member loop (apparently fields), a mixed-kind member is skipped after MsgPack005 is reported. No new test exercises this loop.

claims.text: The analyzer test file header sets up usings, the VerifyCS alias for MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer with its code fix provider, and a shared Preamble.
The README adds a section that documents opting out of source generation and lists which analyzer rules apply to suppressed types. MsgPack012 is listed as applying, but no new test checks it.

In the first member loop, after reporting MsgPack005 (DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys) for a member whose key kind differs from the others, the member is skipped. This avoids dereferencing a null intKey/stringKey later in the loop.

findings.description: `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` throws IndexOutOfRangeException when the member has no source declaration, for example a member inherited from a type in a referenced assembly. That would bring back the kind of analyzer crash this change is meant to fix. Line 1147 still uses FirstOrDefault()?, so the two loops are now inconsistent.
The second loop's fixes (continue at 1148 and ContainsKey guards at 1163 and 1179) have no test. All new analyzer tests use properties; none use fields with duplicate or mixed keys.

`continue` skips the rest of the loop body for the mismatched member. Any later per-member diagnostics in that body (for example the member-type check MsgPack003 or formatter checks) will no longer be reported for that member.

No visible code branches on SuppressSourceGeneration. The fix assumes the reported regression was an analyzer exception on bad keys. If 3.1.1 also skipped suppressed types somewhere else, or failed for valid suppressed types, the fix may be incomplete. The diff cannot show this.
